A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoGe study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original point-map, depth, and camera-FOV evaluations, ablation experiments, and qualitative reconstructions, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and ablations and includes additional qualitative comparisons and a failure example.

M1.justification: The affine-invariant representation, ROE alignment, local geometry losses, normal and mask supervision, and focal recovery remain the same. Added pseudocode and the change from 'clipping' to 'truncation' elaborate the existing procedure rather than establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 21 training datasets, eight quantitative benchmarks, and first-100-image DIV2K comparison. v2 identifies OpenImagesV7 as the previously unspecified retrieval-reference dataset; unchanged training mixtures support treating this as additional documentation.

E2.justification: Figure 7 now includes Metric3D V2 and Depth Anything V2 point-cloud comparisons for its in-the-wild examples, where v1 marked those 3D outputs unavailable. These methods already participated in v1's separate DIV2K comparison. Quantitative comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated relative point-error and inlier normalization from the predicted-point norm to the ground-truth-point norm. This is a reported metric correction; unchanged point-map scores do not establish that evaluation was rerun. Existing splits, preprocessing, and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a thin-structure failure case in Figure 9, showing a fence reconstructed as flattened geometry. The representation, alignment, local-loss, and mask ablations retain their earlier evidence; the added truncation discussion refers to an existing ablation row.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing mean and median FOV summaries are unchanged.

E6.justification: MoGe's average affine-depth rank changes from 1.56 in v1 Table 3 to 1.00 in v2 Table 2. Other benchmark and ablation numbers are retained apart from equivalent rounding. v2 also adds or replaces qualitative comparisons, reports the fence failure, and newly states that truncation improves training stability.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects Lemma 1's zero-residual condition and the derivative-jump expression and inequality in Equation 17. These repair mathematical statements within the existing argument; the principal solver results and approximate 3D-shift assumption remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: affine-invariant monocular geometry, robust global alignment, local supervision, and superior point-map, depth, and FOV estimation. Their substantive scope and headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix D discusses thin-structure failures and temporal inconsistency in monocular video. It attributes thin-structure difficulties to model capacity and noisy training data and explains why video reconstruction would require additional solutions. These applicability qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed solver Algorithms 2–5, specifies the truncation threshold as 1, and explains DINOv2/OpenImagesV7 dataset weighting. New Appendix B.3 documents evaluation alignment objectives and disparity clipping. The abstract also changes code and models from a promised release to reported availability. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Open Images and Kinect sensor evaluation, supporting dataset weighting and the existing depth-range restriction. The central positioning relative to DUSt3R, monocular depth estimation, and camera calibration remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Numerous paragraphs across the introduction, related work, approach, experiments, and conclusion are rewritten and condensed. The appendix is reorganized and expanded with explicit algorithm descriptions, an evaluation-protocol subsection, and limitations. Terminology and prediction-versus-ground-truth notation are also refined.

P2.justification: v2 reworks Figure 7 and adds preprocessing, failure, and expanded comparison displays in Figures 8–11. It merges v1's training-source and loss tables into Table 5 and adds four algorithm boxes. The existing final reconstruction galleries are retained and captioned as Figures 12–13.

improvement.justification: v1 already supplies the central method, derivations, and extensive empirical evidence. v2 makes that study easier to reproduce and assess through explicit evaluation alignment, solver pseudocode, the truncation threshold, and concrete limitations. Rank and mathematical corrections improve accuracy, although inconsistencies remain in Appendix A.2. The net gain is a useful refinement in transparency and presentation.
